docName.remove: Remove this PDF from the project
docName.label: Name of the exported PDF
docName.labelImages: Name of this group of images

toolbar.snap: Snap to the page and to other pieces while dragging (hold Ctrl/Cmd to drag without it)
toolbar.snapEdges: Stick to edges in the artwork while dragging (hold Ctrl/Cmd to drag without it)
toolbar.includeOnePage: Every page is skipped. Include at least one page to export.
toolbar.nothingToPrint: Nothing to print yet. Choose pieces and give them copies.

issues.label: Export problems
issues.fixPrint: Fix these, then export again. Pieces are never scaled to fit.
issues.fixSource: Fix these pages, or skip them, then export again.
issues.fixLocked: Remove this PDF from the project, or ask its publisher for an unlocked version.

warnings.label: Print quality warnings
warnings.blurry: {{name}} will look blurry at this size ({{dpi}} dpi).
warnings.soft: {{name}} may print a little soft ({{dpi}} dpi).
warnings.missing: {{name}} was not found: this page prints blank.
warnings.note: These do not stop the export.

viewport.openHint: Open a PDF to get started (Ctrl/Cmd+O)
viewport.pageSkipped: This page is skipped: it is left out of the export.
viewport.noGuides: Drag from a ruler onto the page to make a guide; drag it back onto its ruler to delete it.

preview.title: Preview
preview.selectRegion: Select the piece region on the page to preview the result.
preview.overflow: Layout exceeds the page by {{width}} horizontally and {{height}} vertically. Pieces are never scaled: change the page size or orientation, or reduce spacing or margins.

gapFields.linked: Linked: both gaps change together. Click to set them separately.
gapFields.unlinked: Not linked: horizontal and vertical are set separately. Click to link them.

source.skippedRange_one: {{range}} is left out of the export.
source.skippedRange_other: {{range}} are left out of the export.
source.dragRegion: Drag on the page to select the region the pieces occupy.
source.gapNote: Gap already between pieces in the PDF.
source.outputNote: The output gap between pieces, the page size and margins, and which pieces go on which sheet, are set in the Print tab.

turnIntoPieces.title: Turns every cell of this grid into a piece of its own, at the same place and size, and clears the region so you can draw the next grid
turnIntoPieces.done_one: 1 piece made. Draw a grid for the next size of piece.
turnIntoPieces.done_other: {{count}} pieces made. Draw a grid for the next size of piece.
turnIntoPieces.none: This grid has no pieces to turn.
turnIntoPieces.shared_one: This page's grid is used by 1 page.
turnIntoPieces.shared_other: This grid is shared by {{count}} pages.
turnIntoPieces.onlyThisPageHint: The page leaves the group; the other pages keep their grid.
turnIntoPieces.everyPageHint: All of them become pieces, and their grid region is cleared.

grids.addTitle: Add another grid to this page, for pieces of another size, then draw its region on the page
grids.full: A page can hold up to {{count}} grids.
grids.note: Each grid has its own region, rows, columns and gap, and can have a name and a color. The Properties panel has the picked grid's settings, and it is the one edited on the page; the others are drawn dimmer, and clicking one picks it. Drag grids and folders in the list to change their order, or drop a grid into a folder. Pick a folder to move its grids together on the page; picking a grid moves it on its own. The page's freeform pieces are listed after the grids. Double-click a name to change it, and click the dot for the color.
grids.name: Grid name
grids.pickFolder: Pick the grids of {{name}}, to move them together
grids.newFolderTitle: New folder: drag grids into it to move them together
grids.emptyFolder: {{name}} is empty: drag grids into it
grids.hide: Hide {{name}} on the page (it still prints)
grids.skipped: This page is skipped: it has no grids.
grids.deleteLast: Clear {{name}}: the last grid loses its region, so it can be drawn again
grids.addColor: Add a color of your own

freeform.title: Freeform pieces
freeform.none: No freeform pieces on this page. They are printed from the Print tab.
freeform.count_one: {{count}} freeform piece on this page. It is printed from the Print tab.
freeform.count_other: {{count}} freeform pieces on this page. They are printed from the Print tab.
freeform.chooseTool: Choose the Select tool (V) or the Piece tool (C) to move, resize or rotate them.
freeform.drawHint: Drag on the page to draw a piece, and click one to edit it. Drag the dot above a piece to rotate it; Shift snaps to 15°. Shift-click picks several, Ctrl+A picks them all, and the arrow keys move what is picked.
freeform.pickedNote: A value typed here goes to every picked piece.

pages.skippedTitle: Skipped: left out of the export
pages.addPdfTitle: Add another PDF to this project. Its pieces join the piece library.
pages.addImagesTitle: Adds PNG, JPEG or WebP images as pieces, one per page.

applyGrid.title: Apply this grid to…
applyGrid.description: Copies the grid and piece region of page {{page}} ({{rows}}×{{columns}}). Each target becomes its own group, so you can then edit it on its own.
applyGrid.onlyThisPage: Only this page (detach it from its group)
applyGrid.sameSize: All pages of the same size (skipped pages stay skipped)
applyGrid.skippedNoGrid: This page is skipped, so it has no grid to copy.
applyGrid.descriptionSeveral: Copies grids and their piece regions from page {{page}}. Each target becomes its own group, so you can edit it separately afterwards.

library.openPdf: Open a PDF to see its pieces.
library.makePortraitTitle: Turn the selected pieces that are wider than tall, so they are all portrait
library.makeLandscapeTitle: Turn the selected pieces that are taller than wide, so they are all landscape
library.modeAll: Every piece prints once. Change the copies of a piece to print a custom selection.
library.modeCustom: Only pieces with copies are printed.
library.emptyNone: No pieces yet. Draw the piece region on a page in the Source tab.

thumb.label: p{{page}} · {{position}}
thumb.title: Page {{page}}, {{position}} · {{size}}
thumb.commonBack: Common back of the pieces without one

library.pickingBack: Click the piece to use as the back of the selection. Esc cancels.

error.note: Pieces are never scaled. Change the page, spacing or margins, or auto-fit the page.

plan.allHint: Every piece once, as the source lays them out.
plan.customHint: Only the pieces you give copies, e.g. 4 × A, 2 × B, 3 × C.
plan.autoFillHint: Repeat the pieces until the last sheet is full.
plan.groupedHint: A A A A, B B, C C C
plan.interleavedHint: A B C, A B C, A C, A
plan.orderNote: The order only matters when the sheet grid is not the source's.

sheet.sameNote: “Same as source” is for all pieces in order, as the page has them: no auto-fill, and no freeform, turned, resized or reordered pieces. Auto is used instead.
sheet.groupBySizeHint: Pieces of different sizes get their own sheets. Off: one shared grid, slots as large as the largest piece.
sheet.outputGapNote: Final gap between pieces. Independent of the source gap.

selected.title: Selected pieces
selected.empty: Select pieces in the piece library to turn them or set their real size.
selected.backToPage: Back to the size on the page
selected.sameNote: Setting a width or height keeps the piece's shape. 100% is the size on the page.
selected.differNote: These pieces differ in size: set a percentage, or select pieces of one size to give a real size.
selected.linkedHint: Linked: width and height keep the piece's proportions. Click to set them separately.
selected.unlinkedHint: Not linked: width and height are set separately, so the piece can be stretched. Click to link them.

marks.onBacksHint: Puts marks around the backs too, for backs you cut on their own: printed on separate sheets, or glued to the other side of a board. Leave it off to cut through both sides from the front.
marks.innerCrossesHint: Corner marks where the gaps between pieces cross, in line with the ticks in the margins, so the inside can be cut without laying a ruler across the whole sheet. Each piece corner gets two arms along its edges, the mark length or the gap if that is less, so a narrow gap shows a small square. Gaps narrower than the line get none.
marks.note: Marks are printed on the front sheets, and on the back sheets if you ask. Ticks start past the bleed.

bleed.mirrorNote: The edge strip of each piece is drawn again, flipped over the edge. It stays vector.
bleed.sourceNote: Uses what the source PDF has between pieces. Needs at least this much space between them there.
bleed.edgeNote: Each piece's bleed is filled with the most common color along its edge, worked out on this computer. A plain vector fill, good for borders of one color; a piece whose edge has none yet is mirrored.
bleed.note: Pieces keep their size: the bleed is extra art around each one. Leave room for it in the output gap and the margins.
bleed.aiNote: An image model paints the bleed of each piece from a picture of it, continuing its art past the edge. Only the band outside the piece is kept, and the piece itself is still printed from the original, as vector. The pictures are saved in a folder beside the project file. A piece without one is mirrored.

background.sheetHint: Fills the whole sheet with a color before anything is printed on it, so the paper round the pieces is that color. A dark sheet uses a lot of ink.
background.piecesHint: A rectangle of this color under each piece and its bleed, so corners and edges the art leaves empty are filled.
background.note: Plain colors printed under the art. They only show where the source leaves the page empty, and they stay vector.

colors.label: Colors
colors.hint: RGB is right for printing at home and for most online print services. CMYK is for a print shop that asks for it.
colors.cmykNote: Cut marks, plain colors, images added as pieces and Fill with AI pictures are written in CMYK for coated paper (FOGRA39), with black and gray on black ink only. Source PDFs keep their own colors, and the preview still shows screen colors.

duplex.onHint: Prints each piece's back: on a back sheet after every front sheet (duplex), or beside the front to fold (gutterfold).
duplex.offsetNote: Moves everything on the back sheets, to correct the printer's drift between sides. Right and down are positive.
duplex.foldNote: Where the back goes next to its front. The dashed line between them is where to fold; cut around the pair.
duplex.backTurnNote: Following the fold, a back to the right stays as printed and a back below is turned upside down, so it reads the right way once folded.
duplex.foldGapNote: Space between a front and its back. 0 puts the fold on the edge of both; a little helps with thick paper.
duplex.pairsNote: Fold: each back is folded behind its front, with a dashed line at the fold and cut marks around the pair. Cut apart: the front and the back stay two pieces side by side, for quick builds that are not double-sided: no fold line, and cut marks around each.
duplex.backPlaceNote: Where the back goes next to its front. Cut marks go around the front and the back each, and along the line between them.
duplex.backTurnApartNote: A back that is cut apart is printed as it is in the file. Turn it upside down if the file has it that way.
duplex.apartGapNote: Space between a front and its back. 0 puts them edge to edge, with one cut along the line they share.
duplex.useSelected: Use the selected piece as common back
duplex.backNote: A piece with no back of its own gets the common back; with neither, its back stays empty.

calibration.title: Calibration sheet
calibration.intro: Many printers move the back of a sheet by a millimeter or two. This sheet shows by how much, so the backs line up with the fronts.
calibration.step1: Save the sheet and print it on both sides of one piece of paper, at actual size (100%, not “fit to page”). Use the same paper and printer settings as for your pieces.
calibration.step2: Hold the paper up to a light with the back facing you. At each crosshair of the front, see where its lines cross the rulers of the back.
calibration.step3: Type the numbers where the lines cross the rulers: the horizontal ruler gives X, the vertical one Y. Numbers to the right and downward are positive.
calibration.cornersNote: Read the center first. If the corners give clearly different numbers, the printer also turns or scales the back, and an offset cannot fix that.
calibration.replaces: These numbers replace the current back offset.

pairing.openHint: Finds the back of every piece from where it is in the file, instead of picking each one.
pairing.title: Pair backs automatically
pairing.text: Where are the backs in the file?

rules.alternatingHint: Fronts on one page, their backs on the next: page 1 with 2, 3 with 4…
rules.afterFrontsHint: All the front pages first, then all the back pages in the same order.
rules.beside: Beside each other on the page
rules.besideHint: Fronts in one half of each page, backs in the other, to fold (gutterfold).
rules.otherPdfHint: Page 1 of the fronts with page 1 of the backs, page 2 with 2…, piece by piece.

ai.title: By picture, with AI
ai.hint: AI looks at every piece and finds its back, for backs no rule can find: a back per deck, or backs in another order.
ai.sends: Sends a small picture of every piece to {{provider}}
ai.ask: Nothing is sent until you press Find backs with AI. You can check the pairs in the piece library after applying.

pairing.commonBack: Use it as the common back
pairing.commonBackHint: That PDF is one single piece: it becomes the back of every front, instead of only those on page 1.
pairing.common: Every front gets that piece as its back.
pairing.mirrored: Backs are mirrored left to right
pairing.mirroredHint: Usual in double-sided files: the back of the first column is in the last, so it lands behind its front when the paper is turned over.
pairing.upsideDownHint: Turns every back a half turn so it faces like its front. Usual when the backs are below the fronts.
pairing.none: No pairs found with this rule.
pairing.note: Only the fronts are printed; each brings its back. Pieces left without a pair keep what they had.

warnings.marks_off_page: Some cut marks fall outside the page: leave larger margins.
warnings.gap_too_narrow_for_line: A gap is too narrow for a line, or there is none: use ticks or widen the output gap.
warnings.bleed_overlaps_neighbour: The bleeds of neighbouring pieces overlap: make the output gap at least twice the bleed.
warnings.bleed_off_page: The bleed goes past the edge of the page: leave larger margins.
warnings.back_size_differs: A back is not the same size as its front, so the cuts will not line up.
warnings.bleed_exceeds_source_gap: The source has less space between some pieces than the bleed.

aiFill.title: Fill with AI
aiFill.count: {{count}} of {{total}} pieces have an AI fill; the rest are mirrored.
aiFill.text: Each piece is sent as a picture with a magenta frame where the bleed goes, and the image model paints the frame. You see every result before anything is kept.
aiFill.what_one: {{count}} piece will be sent to {{host}} as a picture of about {{size}} px, for the image model {{model}}: one paid image request.
aiFill.what_other: {{count}} pieces will be sent to {{host}} as pictures of about {{size}} px, for the image model {{model}}: {{count}} paid image requests, one each.

blocked.saveFirst: Save the project first: the pictures are kept in a folder beside the project file.
blocked.needsImages: Fill with AI sends pictures of the pieces. Turn on “Send page images” in Preferences › AI Mode.
blocked.noProvider: {{provider}} cannot draw pictures. Choose Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible server in Preferences › AI Mode.
blocked.noModel: Choose an image model in Preferences › AI Mode.
blocked.noPieces: There are no pieces to fill.
blocked.tooMany: Select at most {{max}} pieces in the library ({{count}} now): each one is a paid request.

aiFill.review: Tick the fills to keep. The piece on the right is drawn over its new bleed, as it will print.

sheets.openPdf: Open a PDF to plan the sheets.
sheets.nothing: Nothing to print yet. Choose pieces in the piece library and give them copies, or switch the plan back to all pieces.
sheets.referencesHint: Shows each piece's reference (page and position) on the sheet, to find it in the piece library. Only on screen: the exported PDF does not have them.

general.unitNote: Only changes how lengths are shown and typed. The document itself is never altered.
general.languageNote: Changes apply immediately. System follows the language of your computer.
general.decimalNote: Only changes how numbers are shown. Number fields accept both 63.5 and 63,5 whatever this is set to, and sums such as 12/3.

workspace.visibleNote: The view switcher shows these, in this order. At least one must stay enabled.
workspace.defaultNote: Used when a document opens. Switching views while editing does not change it.
workspace.layoutNote: Changes apply immediately. The Panels menu in the toolbar can always bring a hidden panel back.
workspace.resetNote: Restores panel positions and sizes, the visible views and the default view. Units, language, theme and Live Preview are kept.
workspace.invertRulersHint: Drag from a ruler for a guide across it instead of along it.
workspace.selectAfterGrid: Select tool after drawing a grid
workspace.selectAfterGridHint: Switches to the Select tool once a grid is drawn.

livePreview.title: Live preview
livePreview.manualHint: The preview updates only when you press Refresh preview.
livePreview.note: With Manual, the Preview view refreshes each time you open it, and the Split view has a refresh button (a dot on it means the preview is out of date). Changing this applies to the open document immediately.

about.title: About
about.openBrowser: This will open your web browser at:
about.openFailed: The link could not be opened.
about.licenseNote: Free for personal and noncommercial use. For any commercial use, or if you're not sure whether your use counts, contact joaquinarruiz@gmail.com. The software comes as is, without warranty.
about.licenseFailed: The license text could not be loaded.
about.downloadPageNote: Every version for every system, if you need to download Gutterberg again.

footer.confirm: Reset all preferences? This restores the default application settings. Your document is not affected.

help.welcomeNote: A short tour of the app, in four clips.
help.tipsOff: Help tips are off. Turn on “Show help tips” to see them again.
help.tipsHidden_one: {{count}} help tip is hidden because you closed it. Show it again to see it.
help.tipsHidden_other: {{count}} help tips are hidden because you closed them. Show them again to see them.
help.bugIntro: If something doesn't work, open an issue on GitHub (you need a free GitHub account) and tell us:
help.bugVersion: which version you use and on which system (the button below copies it)
help.bugSteps: what you did, step by step, so someone else can make it happen again
help.bugExpected: what you expected, and what happened instead
help.bugWorkaround: whether you found a way around it
help.bugLog: the log, if the app closed by itself or showed an error (the Copy log button copies it)
help.infoUnavailable: The app info is only available in the app window.
help.logNote: The log is plain text about what the app did and any error it hit. It does not include your PDFs, but an error can mention a file or folder name, so look it over before you send it.
help.logFailed: Couldn't read or copy the log.
help.copyFailed: Couldn't copy. Select the text above and copy it yourself.
help.tutorialsNote: Step-by-step walkthroughs that you start when you need them. Picking one closes Preferences.

updates.versionUnknown: The version is not available here.
updates.failed: Couldn't check for updates. Check your connection and try again.
updates.lastCheckFailed: The last check couldn't reach the update server. Check your connection.
updates.installed: {{version}} is installed. Restart Gutterberg to use it.
updates.notifyFeaturesHint: A new version with new features; fixes alone stay quiet.
updates.notifyNeverHint: Gutterberg doesn't check by itself. Use Check for updates when you want to.
updates.tellMeNote: Gutterberg checks once a day and this only decides whether a message appears; with Never it doesn't check at all. This section shows a newer version once a check finds one, and updating installs the newest.

experimental.title: Experimental features
experimental.note: May change or disappear in a later version. Off unless you switch them on.

hintUi.offText: To see them again, turn on “Show help tips” in Preferences › Help.

mark.title: Mark the pieces
mark.text: Drag a rectangle around all the pieces on the page.

grid.title: Set the grid
grid.text: Enter how many columns and rows of pieces there are.

overlay.title: Check the overlay
overlay.text: The grid lines should sit on the pieces. If not, drag the rectangle's handles to adjust it.

goPrint.title: Go to Print
goPrint.text: Open the Print tab to choose which pieces go on which sheet.

one.title: One piece at a time
one.text: Drag on the page to draw a piece, and click a piece to edit it: drag its body to move it, its handles to resize it and the dot above it to rotate it (Shift snaps to 15°). These pieces are printed from the Print tab.

main.text: Live preview is off, so this preview isn't generated automatically. Press the refresh button (bottom right) to generate it. You can change this in Preferences › Display.

Live preview is off, so the row of sheet previews above is not redrawn as you change the plan. Press the refresh button (top right) to update it. The large sheet always follows the plan. You can change this in Preferences › Display.

library.title: Choose pieces
library.text: Pick the pieces you want in the piece library.

copies.title: Set copies
copies.text: Give each piece the number of copies you need, or keep “All pieces in order” to print every piece once.

sheet.title: Sheet and page
sheet.text: Adjust the sheet layout, spacing and page in the print settings.

export.title: Export
export.text: When the sheets look right, export the PDF.

one.title: Grids and pieces on one page
one.text: A page can have several grids and any number of pieces drawn one by one. For three sizes on a page: draw a grid, press Add grid under Grids, draw the next one, and so on.

one.title: Move the region
one.text: Drag the region to move it, or its handles to resize it. Once you have clicked it, the arrow keys move it 1 mm at a time (Shift: 10 mm). Its edges snap to the page and to the pieces; the magnet in the toolbar turns that off.

one.title: Sticky edges
one.text: That side stuck to an edge in the artwork. It stays there for a few pixels, then lets go if you keep dragging. Hold Ctrl/Cmd to drag freely, or turn sticky edges off with this button.

document.title: Open a PDF first
document.text: This tutorial works on a PDF that is open. Open one, and the tutorial goes on from here.

pieces.title: Mark some pieces first
pieces.text: This tutorial needs pieces to work on, and none are marked yet. The “Mark pieces and export” tutorial shows how.

goPrint.title: Open the Print tab
goPrint.text: This is done in the Print tab. Open it from the tabs at the top.

goSource.title: Open the Source tab
goSource.text: This is done in the Source tab, where the pieces are marked on the pages. Open it from the tabs at the top.

resize-pieces.title: Make pieces bigger or smaller
resize-pieces.summary: Give pieces a real size or a percentage, without touching the PDF.

pick.title: Pick the pieces
pick.text: Click the piece you want to resize in the piece library. Select all picks every piece shown, and the selected ones are resized together.

size.title: Set the size
size.text: In Selected pieces, type a new Width or Height: the other side follows while the chain between them is linked. Or type a Scale in percent: 100% is the size on the page.

sheet.title: Check the sheet
sheet.text: The sheet preview shows the pieces at their new size. Pieces are never shrunk to fit: if they do not fit, you get a message to change the sheet instead. “Back to the size on the page” undoes it.

align-backs.title: Line up fronts and backs
align-backs.summary: Correct the printer's drift between the two sides of a sheet with a calibration sheet.

duplex.title: Turn on the backs
duplex.text: Open the Duplex section, turn on Print backs and keep Backs on “On the other side”. In Flip on, choose the edge your printer turns the paper over on.

calibrate.title: Print the calibration sheet
calibrate.text: Press Calibration sheet…, then Save the sheet… and print it on both sides of one piece of paper at actual size (100%, not “fit to page”), with the same paper and printer settings as for your pieces. If you don't see the button, check that Backs is “On the other side”.

read.title: Read the two numbers
read.text: Hold the paper up to a light with the back facing you. See where the lines of the front's crosshair cross the rulers of the back, and type the numbers in the dialog: the horizontal ruler gives X, the vertical one Y, and right and down are positive. Then press Apply.

offset.title: Check Back offset
offset.text: Apply puts the numbers in Back offset X and Y. Print your pieces again and see whether the backs line up; you can fine-tune the offset here by hand.

gutterfold.title: Print gutterfold, or turn it into double-sided
gutterfold.summary: Print each back beside its front to fold or cut apart, or pair the backs and print double-sided.

backs.title: Print the backs beside the fronts
backs.text: Open the Duplex section, turn on Print backs and set Backs to “Beside the front”: each back is printed next to its front, to fold (gutterfold).

pairs.title: Fold or cut apart
pairs.text: Pairs says what each front and back become. Fold keeps them as one piece, with a dashed line at the fold and cut marks around the pair. Cut apart leaves them as two pieces side by side, with no fold line, for quick builds that are not double-sided. Fold (Back, when cut apart) sets whether the back goes to the right or below.

double.title: Or make it double-sided
double.text: If your file has the backs beside the fronts and you want a double-sided print instead, press Pair backs automatically…, choose “Beside each other on the page” and Apply, then set Backs to “On the other side”.

pair-backs.title: Pair fronts with their backs
pair-backs.summary: Let Gutterberg find each piece's back from where it is in the file.

open.title: Open the pairing
open.text: Open the Duplex section, turn on Print backs and press Pair backs automatically….

rule.title: Say where the backs are
rule.text: Under “Where the backs are”, pick the rule that matches your file: Alternating pages (page 1 with 2, 3 with 4…), Backs after fronts, Beside each other on the page, or Backs in another PDF. Options such as mirrored or upside-down backs appear when they apply. Press Apply when the dialog counts the pairs you expect.

check.title: Check the pairs
check.text: A piece with a back shows it in the piece library, and Selected pieces › Back says which one it is. Pieces left without a pair keep what they had; select one and use Pick back… to set its back by hand.

paper-size.title: Choose the paper size
paper-size.summary: Print on A4, Letter, A3 or another size, in portrait or landscape.

size.title: Choose the paper
size.text: In the Sheet section, open Size and choose the paper: A4, Letter, A3, A5, Legal, Tabloid / Ledger, Custom, Same as source or Auto-fit to pieces. Pieces keep their size whichever you pick.

orientation.title: Portrait or landscape
orientation.text: In the Page section, Orientation turns the sheet (it isn't there for Same as source or Auto-fit to pieces). The margins are there too, and the sheet preview shows the result.

cut-marks.title: Add cut marks
cut-marks.summary: Print lines that show where to cut, solid, dashed or dotted.

style.title: Choose where the marks go
style.text: Open the Cut marks section and choose a Style: Ticks in the margins draws short lines at every edge, outside the pieces; Lines in the gaps runs a line down the middle of each gap between them.

line.title: Solid, dashed or dotted
line.text: Choose how the line is drawn: Solid, Dashed or Dotted. Line width and Color are below, and ticks also have a length and a distance from the piece.

sheet.title: Check the sheet
sheet.text: The sheet preview draws the marks as they will print. They go on the front sheets only. If a gap is too narrow for a line, or marks fall outside the page, the Cut marks section says so and how to fix it.

find-piece.title: Find a piece on the sheet
find-piece.summary: Show each piece's reference on the sheet and look it up in the piece library.

show.title: Show the references
show.text: Press Show piece references above the sheet to write each piece's reference (its page and position, like p3 · r1 c2) on it. It is only on screen: the exported PDF doesn't have them.

library.title: Find it in the library
library.text: The piece library shows the same reference under each piece. Click that piece to select it and change its copies, size or back.

several-grids.title: Mark pieces of different sizes on one page
several-grids.summary: Draw one grid for each size of piece on the same page.

first.title: Mark the first size
first.text: Choose the Grid tool (G), drag a rectangle round the pieces of one size, and set its columns and rows.

add.title: Add the next grid
add.text: Press Add grid in the Grids and pieces panel, then drag a rectangle round the pieces of the next size. A page can hold up to 9 grids.

name.title: Name and color them
name.text: Double-click a grid's name in the list to rename it, and click the dot at its left to choose its color. Each grid keeps its own rows, columns and gap.

pick.title: Pick either one
pick.text: With the Select tool (V), press any grid on the page to pick it, drag it or resize it from its handles. Pressing its name in the list picks it too.

images-as-pieces.title: Use images as pieces
images-as-pieces.summary: Turn image files, such as scans or card art, into pieces of a size you choose.

open.title: Add the images
open.text: Open the File menu and choose Add images…, or drag the image files onto the window.

size.title: Choose the size
size.text: Under Piece size, choose the size the images print at (a preset, the size the image says it is, or Custom) and say whether they include bleed. Images are never stretched or resampled. Press Add images.

library.title: They are pieces now
library.text: Each image is a piece in the piece library of the Print tab, ready to get copies, a back and a place on the sheets.

mark-and-export.title: Mark pieces and export
mark-and-export.summary: From a PDF to cut-ready sheets: mark the pieces, choose copies and export.

update.title: Update Gutterberg
update.summary: Check for a newer version and install it.

open.title: Open Updates
open.text: Preferences › Updates shows the version you have.

check.title: Check for updates
check.text: Press Check for updates. It says if you are up to date.

install.title: Install it
install.text: If a newer version is available, it is listed with what's new. Press Download and install, and Restart now when it is ready. If the project has changes that are not saved, Gutterberg asks to save them first.

report-problem.title: Report a problem
report-problem.summary: Copy the log and open the GitHub form with your version filled in.

menu.title: Open Report a problem
menu.text: Open the ? Help menu and choose Report a problem. It opens Preferences › About, on “Found a bug?”.

log.title: Copy the log
log.text: If the app closed by itself or showed an error, press Copy log. It has no PDFs, but an error can mention a file name, so look it over before you share it. Copy app info copies the version and system.

form.title: Report it on GitHub
form.text: Press Report on GitHub. After asking, it opens the issue form in your browser with your version and system filled in. Say what you did, step by step, what you expected, and paste the log.

errors.does_not_fit: The laid-out pieces need {{needed_w_mm}} × {{needed_h_mm}} mm but the sheet is only {{page_w_mm}} × {{page_h_mm}} mm.
errors.page_out_of_range: Page {{page}} does not exist (the document has {{count}} pages).
errors.unsupported_rotation: Page {{page}} has a rotation of {{rotate}}°; only multiples of 90° are supported.
errors.unsupported_user_unit: Page {{page}} has a /UserUnit of {{unit}}; only 1 is supported.
errors.superseded: A newer request replaced this one.
errors.worker_stopped: The renderer stopped. Restart the app.
errors.same_file: Choose a different file than the one that is open.
errors.no_pages: No pages are included in the export.
errors.internal: Something went wrong inside the app: {{detail}}
errors.freeform_only: This page has only freeform pieces: print it from the Print tab.
errors.not_a_project: This is not a valid project file.
errors.project_too_new: This project was made with a newer version of the app (file version {{found}}; this version reads up to {{supported}}). Please update.
errors.project_invalid: This project file is damaged or incomplete.
errors.bleed_exceeds_source_gap: The source has {{gap_mm}} mm between some pieces, less than the {{bleed_mm}} mm of bleed taken from it.
errors.ai_pdf_locked: This PDF's publisher restricted it, so AI Mode doesn't send its pages anywhere. Mark the pieces by hand or with Detect pieces.
errors.ai_no_key: No API key is saved for this provider. Add one in Preferences › AI Mode.
errors.ai_keychain: The system keychain could not be used: {{detail}}
errors.ai_timeout: The provider did not answer in time.
errors.ai_invalid_reply: The reply could not be read: {{detail}}. Nothing was changed.
errors.ai_invalid_proposal: The proposal does not fit: {{detail}}. Nothing was changed.
errors.ai_text_only_needs_objects: This page has no objects to describe. Turn on “Send page images” in Preferences › AI Mode.
errors.ai_pairing_needs_images: Pair backs with AI looks at the pieces, so it needs pictures. Turn on “Send page images” in Preferences › AI Mode.
errors.ai_too_many_pieces: There are {{count}} pieces, and Pair backs with AI can look at {{max}} at most. Skip the pages you don't need in the Source tab, or pair with a rule.
errors.image_unsupported: “{{name}}” can't be used. Images can be PNG, JPEG or WebP.
errors.image_too_large: “{{name}}” is too large ({{megapixels}} megapixels, {{mb}} MB). The limits are 100 megapixels and 200 MB.
errors.pdf_locked: This PDF's publisher doesn't allow changes. Contact them for an unlocked print-and-play version.
errors.ai_fill_needs_images: Fill with AI sends pictures of the pieces. Turn on “Send page images” in Preferences › AI Mode.
errors.ai_no_image_output: This provider cannot draw pictures. Use Gemini or an OpenAI-compatible server for Fill with AI.
errors.fill_reply: The picture that came back cannot be used ({{detail}}).
errors.fill_tilted: This piece is tilted on its page; Fill with AI works on straight pieces only.

presets.title: Presets
presets.none: No presets yet. Save the current grid to reuse it on other page groups.
presets.applyTitle: Sets the rows, columns and source gap of the pages that share this grid
presets.name: Preset name
presets.saveTitle: Save the rows, columns and source gap of this page group under this name

close.message: Save the changes to “{{name}}” before closing?
close.messageNew: This project has never been saved. Save it before closing?

share.done: Saved, with “{{readme}}” beside it. To share the project, give the project file, the readme and its PDFs together, in one folder.
share.elsewhere: These files are in another folder. Put a copy of them beside the project before you share it: {{files}}

readme.title: {{project}}: a Gutterberg project
readme.what: This folder has a print-and-play game and a Gutterberg project for it ({{project}}). Gutterberg is a free desktop app that turns print-and-play PDFs into sheets that are easy to cut: every piece at its exact size, with space between them, and the original artwork untouched.
readme.ready: The project already has every piece marked and a print layout chosen, so there is nothing to set up.
readme.step1: Download Gutterberg from {{link}} and install it.
readme.step2: Keep these files together in one folder:
readme.step4: Go to the Print tab, check the sheets, and click Export PDF to save a PDF ready to print.
readme.change: You can change anything before exporting: copies, paper size, gaps, cut marks, bleed and backs.

share.fills: The bleed uses pictures from Fill with AI: share the folder “{{folder}}” too, next to the project file.

recovery.message: Gutterberg closed with unsaved changes to “{{name}}”. Restore them?
recovery.messageNew: Gutterberg closed with unsaved work on a project that was never saved. Restore it?

discard.message: This project has changes that are not saved. Discard them?

remove.message: Remove “{{name}}” from the project? Its pieces leave the piece library and the sheets. The file on disk is not touched.
remove.messageLast: This is the only PDF of the project. Remove “{{name}}”? The project will be left empty. The file on disk is not touched.

relink.message: Where is “{{name}}” now? Choose the PDF to keep opening the project.
relink.differs: This file is not the same as the PDF “{{name}}” the project was saved with, so the pieces may not be where they were. Use it anyway?

notices.label: Project messages
notices.pdfChanged: “{{name}}” has changed since the project was saved. Check that the pieces are still where you marked them.
notices.layoutReset: “{{name}}” has a different number of pages than when the project was saved, so its page groups and pieces were reset.
notices.imageChanged: “{{name}}” has changed since the project was saved. Its page now shows the new image.
notices.imagesMissing: Some images of “{{name}}” were not found. Their pages stay blank until you add the images again.
notices.fillsMissing_one: {{count}} AI fill picture was not found beside the project. Its piece gets a mirrored bleed until you fill it again.
notices.fillsMissing_other: {{count}} AI fill pictures were not found beside the project. Their pieces get a mirrored bleed until you fill them again.

detect.note: Proposes where the pieces are on this page, found on your computer. Nothing changes until you apply it.
detect.none: No pieces found on this page. Draw the region by hand.
detect.onThePage: The proposal is on the page: check the outlines, then apply it.
detect.lowWarning: Low confidence: check the outlines before applying.

notes.missing_cells: Some places of the grid have no object: the last row may not be full.
notes.crop_marks: Cut marks in the margins line up with the grid.
notes.few_objects: Only a few objects back this, so check it.
notes.touches_edge: A piece touches the edge of the page.
notes.merged_pieces: Some shapes were not clean rectangles: pieces that touch cannot be told apart.
notes.no_regular_pattern: The art seems to run across the piece borders, so no regular pattern shows.

models.count_one: {{count}} model from {{host}}, saved on {{date}}. Type to search, or type any model id.
models.count_other: {{count}} models from {{host}}, saved on {{date}}. Type to search, or type any model id.
models.refreshFailed: Showing the list saved on {{date}}: it couldn't be loaded again. {{error}}
models.empty: {{host}} listed no models. Type the model id.
models.failed: Couldn't load the list of models; type the model id. {{error}}
models.needsKey: Save a key to pick from the provider's models, or type the model id.
models.reload: Ask the provider for its list of models again

modelHint.anthropic: A Claude model id, e.g. claude-sonnet-5-5 or claude-haiku-5-5.
modelHint.openai_compatible: A model that reads images, with the address of its server, e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1, https://api.x.ai/v1 or http://localhost:1234/v1.
modelHint.gemini: A Gemini model id, e.g. gemini-2.5-flash.
modelHint.ollama: A vision model you have pulled, e.g. llava or llama3.2-vision.

settings.title: AI Mode (experimental)
settings.enableNote: Adds AI buttons that send pages to a provider you choose, with your own key. Off by default. Nothing is sent unless you press one; while it is on, choosing a provider here asks it for its list of models.
settings.baseUrlNote: Leave empty for the provider's own address. Plain http is only accepted for this computer or a private network.
settings.keySaved: A key is saved in the system keychain.
settings.keyReplace: Paste a new key to replace it
settings.keyNote: The key goes straight to the system keychain. It is never shown again and never saved in a project or in these preferences.
settings.sendImagesOff: Text only: no picture is ever sent. The model gets sizes, counts of objects and the start of each page's text.
settings.askFirstOn: Before every AI action, a notice shows what will be sent and to which server, and waits for Send.
settings.askFirstOff: No notice for {{host}}: AI actions send right away. A different provider or address is asked about again.
settings.testOk: Connected. Used {{input}} input and {{output}} output tokens.
settings.workspaceNote: Only for an API key that is not scoped to a workspace: the ID of the workspace to use, sent as the anthropic-workspace-id header. Leave empty otherwise.
settings.testSends: Sends a short test message to {{provider}}

confirm.title: Send to {{provider}}?
confirm.detectImage: Page {{page}} will be sent as a picture, about {{size}} px on its long side.
confirm.detectText: Text only: no picture is sent. The model gets the page size and the boxes of its images and rectangles.
confirm.sortImages: {{count}} pages ({{range}}) will be sent as small pictures, about {{size}} px, in {{requests}} requests.
confirm.sortText: Text only: no picture is sent. {{count}} pages ({{range}}) are described to the model (size, counts of objects, start of the text) in {{requests}} requests.
confirm.pairImages: {{count}} pieces will be sent as small pictures, about {{size}} px each, in one request.
confirm.dontAsk: Don't ask again before sending to {{host}}

detect.note: Asks the AI provider where the pieces are on this page. Nothing changes until you apply the proposal.

sort.title: Sort pages
sort.note: Labels every page (pieces, backs, rules, cover, other) so pages without pieces can be skipped. Nothing changes until you apply it.
sort.sends: Sends the pages of this PDF to {{provider}}

experimental.title: AI Mode is experimental
experimental.text: AI Mode still needs further testing and may not work as expected. It can be token hungry: every action sends pages to your provider, and the tokens cost money. Use it at your own responsibility.

imageModelHint.anthropic: Claude does not draw pictures, so Fill with AI is not available with it.
imageModelHint.openai_compatible: For Fill with AI: a model that edits images with a mask, e.g. gpt-image-1 on https://api.openai.com/v1.
imageModelHint.gemini: For Fill with AI: a Gemini model that draws images, e.g. gemini-2.5-flash-image.
imageModelHint.ollama: Ollama does not draw pictures, so Fill with AI is not available with it.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.hint: Press ? at any time to open this list.

items.undo: Undo the last change (in either tab)
items.closeDialog: Close a dialog, a menu, an info tip, a help tip or a message
items.nextPage: Next page (the arrow, with nothing picked)
items.previousPage: Previous page (the arrow, with nothing picked)
items.deletePiece: Delete the picked pieces (Select or Piece tool)
items.removePage: Remove a page from view (its thumbnail picked in the Pages panel)
items.snapRotation: Rotate a piece in 15° steps (hold while turning it)
items.selectMore: Add or remove a piece from the selection
items.revertNumber: Go back to the previous number
items.nudgeFine: Raise or lower it in small steps
items.nudgeCoarse: Raise or lower it in big steps
items.nudgePicked: Move the picked region or pieces 1 mm (0.05 in)
items.nudgePickedBig: Move the picked region or pieces 10 mm (0.5 in)
items.pickMore: Add or remove a piece from the picked ones (Select or Piece tool)
items.pickAll: Pick every piece of the page
items.pickNone: Pick nothing (the pieces and the region)
items.duplicatePieces: Duplicate the picked pieces (Select or Piece tool)
items.dragCopy: Drag a copy of the picked pieces, leaving them where they are (Select or Piece tool)
items.dragFree: Drag a region or pieces without snapping or sticking to edges
items.makeGuide: Make a guide: drag from a ruler onto the page (rulers on)
items.deleteGuide: Move a guide, or delete it by dragging it back onto its ruler

start.title: Get started
start.lead: Open a Print-and-Play PDF to space its pieces, or pick up a project.
start.shortcuts: Press ? to see the keyboard shortcuts.

images.changed: “{{name}}” is not the same image the project was saved with. Use it instead?

badge.missingTitle: This image was not found, so this piece is blank.
badge.softTitle: About {{dpi}} dpi at this size: it may print a little soft.
badge.blurryTitle: About {{dpi}} dpi at this size: it will look blurry.

dialog.label: Add images
dialog.lead: Each image becomes a piece. Choose the size it prints at; images are never stretched or resampled.
dialog.fromImageOff: From the image (not every file has a resolution)
dialog.bleedInfo: The page is the piece size plus the bleed on every side, so “bleed from the source” in the Print tab uses the image's own bleed.
dialog.differLead_one: This image is not the shape of the piece. It is never stretched.
dialog.differLead_other: These images are not the shape of the piece. They are never stretched.
dialog.fitHint: Fit shows the whole image with blank margins; Fill covers the piece and cuts off what does not fit.
dialog.soft: {{dpi}} dpi at this size: may print a little soft.
dialog.blurry: {{dpi}} dpi at this size: will look blurry.
dialog.exportSize: Adds about {{size}} to the exported PDF.
dialog.veryLarge: {{dpi}} dpi: much sharper than any printer needs. Adds about {{size}}; the exported PDF will be large.
dialog.reduce: Reduce very large images to 600 dpi
dialog.reduceHint: PNG and WebP images above 600 dpi are shrunk to 600 dpi (still lossless). JPEG images are never reduced: that would mean compressing them again and losing quality. Your files are not touched.

sheetSet.title: Sheet set to {{size}} so the pieces fit
sheetSet.text: An image is the size of one piece, so a sheet the size of the source would hold only that piece. Change it in Print › Sheet.

cut.title: Your PDF, cut into pieces
cut.text: Mark where the pieces are on a page: a grid, Detect pieces, or one by one with the piece tool.

place.title: On the sheet you print
place.text: Pick a sheet size such as A4 or Letter. Your pieces keep their exact size.

arrange.title: Arrange them your way
arrange.text: Put the pieces in the order you want, set the gap between them, and choose which ones to print and how many copies.

done.title: Ready to cut
done.text: Export a PDF with cut marks, bleed or duplex if you want. Your artwork is never changed.

setup.title: Make Gutterberg yours
setup.text: Choose your language, how the app looks and the unit you measure in. Everything starts as your system has it, so you can just continue.
setup.note: You can change all of these any time in Preferences.

updates.unsaved: This project has changes that are not saved. Save them before Gutterberg restarts?

lock.printing: “{{name}}” doesn't allow printing, so it can't be exported. Contact its publisher for an unlocked print-and-play version.
lock.modifying: “{{name}}” doesn't allow changes, so it can't be exported. Contact its publisher for an unlocked print-and-play version.
lock.restrictedNote: “{{name}}” has restrictions from its publisher (for example, copying). The exported PDF keeps them.

sizePresets.label: {{name}}: {{dims}}
sizePresets.title: Size preset
sizePresets.name: Name for this size
sizePresets.saveTitle: Save the size of the first selected piece under this name, to use it on other pieces and in other projects
sizePresets.stretchAsk: Some selected pieces have other proportions than {{name}} ({{size}}), so they will be stretched to that size. To keep their proportions, save or pick a size that fixes only the width or only the height.
